To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
during crowded events, voice and data performance can degrade significantly due to changes in user behavior, application workload, and population distribution.

during crowded events, voice and data traffic volume is orders of magnitude higher, connection failure rates are higher, and connection sharing can significantly reduce connection failures without requiring any infrastructure changes.

(a) the changes in population density and user behavior during crowded events cause more than two orders-of-magnitude increase in connection failures and more than 10 times decrease in average data throughput, (b) more aggressive release of resources and opportunistic connection-sharing can significantly improve voice and data performance during crowded events without requiring costly infrastructure changes, and (c) the performance gains from opportunistic connection-sharing are significant even when only a small fraction of the devices in each cell participate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of improving the performance of cellular networks during crowded events.
understanding and improving cellular network performance in real-life crowded environments.

understanding and improving the performance of cellular networks during crowded events, where network performance is critical to the quality of experience and safety of millions of event participants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the network performance is not degraded during crowded events and that it is not necessary to deploy any special measures.

the cellular network performance is significantly degraded during crowded events, the degradation is mainly caused by changes in the user behavior and the workload during the event, and the two mechanisms of radio resource allocation tuning, and opportunistic connections sharing can significantly mitigate the performance degradation.

the performance of cellular networks during crowded events is highly dependent on the specific crowded event, the cellular network, the user behavior and applications, and the mitigation scheme employed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cellular networks should be designed to handle crowded event traffic by using a combination of infrastructure changes and application level solutions.

we characterize and analyze the performance of cellular networks during crowded events, identify the root causes of performance degradation, and propose two practical mechanisms that can improve the performance of cellular network without resorting to expensive network infrastructure changes.

the cellular network performance during crowded events is much worse than that during routine days, and the performance can be improved significantly by simple tuning of radio resource allocation and by opportunistic connection sharing, both without resorting to expensive infrastructure changes.
The main takeaway from our work is that

cellular networks should be able to dynamically adjust radio resource allocation to adapt to the changing traffic conditions and user behavior, and that opportunistic connection sharing should be supported by cellular network operators and device manufacturers to help improve cellular network performance during crowded events.
the performance degradation of cellular networks during crowded events can be mitigated with practical techniques that are not prohibitively expensive.

the performance of cellular networks during crowded events is fundamentally different from that during routine days, and the design of cellular network management and optimization schemes must be tailored to the specific challenges that arise during crowded events.
